name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,313

entries.clue: S for sovereign? (4,2,5)

blocks.note: looks like an abbreviation to expand; instead it is the letter itself, and the question is which word it begins
a monarch, the figure at the top of a country; the question mark flags the letter play

annotation.surface: A dictionary or style guide listing S as the abbreviation for a sovereign.
annotation.walkthrough: Read S as a letter, not an abbreviation: it is the first letter, the head, of the word STATE, and a sovereign is a head of state.
annotation.definitionFit: A reigning monarch is the formal leader of the country, the title that phrase names.

entries.clue: Earth’s molten core (5)

indicatorNotes.molten: melted down, so the letters flow into a new shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 5 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A geology fact: the centre of our planet is molten.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is true geology, so 'molten core' reads as one phrase; split it, and 'core' alone is the definition. The 's is just 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the heart of a matter or a place is its central part, its core.

entries.clue: Players regularly fancy long hair (9)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals: the 2nd and 4th

blocks.note: the even letters of fAnCy
tresses = long locks of hair

annotation.surface: Performers who happen to fancy long hair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb meaning like; it only supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Players in the theatrical sense are performers on stage, and these are female ones.

entries.clue: Oscar caught by sinister sect involving magic (6)

blocks.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
c = caught, the cricket scorecard abbreviation
a cult is a sinister sect

annotation.surface: Someone called Oscar ensnared by a sinister magical sect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught by' looks like one instruction to put O inside something; instead 'caught' is its own letter, C, and 'by' simply places the pieces side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective covers the supernatural and hidden arts, so practices involving magic are described by it.

entries.clue: Air for example to rise and fall (3)

indicatorNotes.to rise: in a down entry, rising means reading from the bottom up

blocks.note: air is an example of a gas

annotation.surface: Air rising and falling, like warm and cold currents.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rise and fall' reads as one phrase; it splits, with 'to rise' turning GAS over and 'fall' the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of droop or sink, as prices or a ceiling can.

entries.clue: A more suitable accomplice (7)

blocks.note: the article plus a comparative meaning 'more suitable', read as two words
one who helps another commit a crime; the verb behind it is to abet

annotation.surface: A better-qualified partner in crime.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer as A BETTER to get the first sense; the second is one word, someone who abets.
annotation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is an article and a comparative; as one word it is a crime helper.

entries.clue: Footballers on trip securing two hotels, last-minute (8,4)

indicatorNotes.securing: TOUR secures, holds fast, the two Hs

blocks.note: a football team is an eleven
a tour is a trip
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet, twice

annotation.surface: A football team on tour, booking two hotels at the last minute.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a team's travel booking; a football side of eleven players is itself called an eleven.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase, from the parable of labourers hired late in the day, means the last possible moment.

entries.clue: Reckless, putting wicked Mike into welfare supervision (5,3,4)

indicatorNotes.putting: putting is the act of placing something somewhere, here the wicked pieces being set down
indicatorNotes.into: the placed pieces go inside the care phrase

blocks.note: day care = supervised care during the day
wicked = evil
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone recklessly placing a wicked man called Mike in social care.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a social worker's reckless decision; 'welfare supervision' is a roundabout way to describe care for children or the elderly during the day.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone who says 'the devil may care' shrugs off consequences, which is recklessness.

entries.clue: European finally in charge of stretcher (7)

blocks.note: E = European
last = finally
IC = in charge

annotation.surface: A European finally given charge of a hospital stretcher.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stretcher' suggests a hospital, but here it is anything that stretches.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal reading of the definition: material that stretches is a stretcher, not a hospital carrier.

entries.clue: Colour almost ringing black bird (5)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost means not quite all, so the colour stops one letter short
indicatorNotes.ringing: the shortened colour forms a ring around B

blocks.note: GREEN without its last letter
B = black, as on pencils

annotation.surface: A shade that nearly surrounds a black bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Black bird' reads as one creature; black gives only B and bird is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a diving water bird known for its courtship dances.

entries.clue: Expecting not to have been blackballed? (2,3,4)

blocks.note: pregnant, in a British slang phrase
a blackball is a vote to refuse someone membership of a society

annotation.surface: A would-be member hoping their club application wasn't rejected.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the club' is British slang for pregnant; the second sense is literal membership, with the question mark flagging the whimsy.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang for pregnant, and literally a member who was not voted out.

entries.clue: Sausage exploded covering nasty wart (9)

indicatorNotes.covering: BURST covers, goes around, the other letters
indicatorNotes.nasty: the letters of WART are messed up

blocks.note: burst = exploded
WART rearranged

annotation.surface: A sausage that bursts on the grill, over something grim.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exploded' reads as the sausage splitting on a grill, which is why the container word sits so comfortably in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a German pork sausage, usually grilled.

entries.clue: Row, missing last cup game (3)

indicatorNotes.missing last: missing its last means lacking its final letter

blocks.note: a row, as of seats in a theatre or a layer of a wedding cake

annotation.surface: A rowing race missing its last cup match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel or an oar stroke; here it is a tier. A cup tie is a British term for a knockout-cup football match.
annotation.definitionFit: A British sporting term: a match in a knockout cup competition is called a cup tie.

entries.clue: Ponder about one’s bad handling (6)

indicatorNotes.about: MUSE goes around the other letters

blocks.note: to muse is to ponder
one = I, plus the 's

annotation.surface: Someone reflecting on their own mishandling of things.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives two letters: one is I, and the 's stays as S.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: using something wrongly is handling it badly.

entries.clue: Ridiculing racist, I broadcast (7)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: scattered, as seed is broadcast, so the letters spread into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A presenter mocking a racist on air.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' paints a radio show; its job is to scatter the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: writing that holds its targets up to mockery is ridiculing them.

entries.clue: Root cause of rusty vehicle? (6)

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
rot is decay, what makes metal rusty

annotation.surface: Asking what really lies behind a rusting car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Root cause' reads as one phrase; 'Root' alone is the definition, and car rot names the vehicle's decay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the orange vegetable is a taproot.

entries.clue: Sound of military band low, needing to rise? I’m disgusted (6)

indicatorNotes.needing to rise: in a down entry, rising means reading from the bottom up

blocks.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
pah! is an exclamation of disgust

annotation.surface: A listener disgusted by a brass band's droning bass that needs to be lifted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like a deep note, fitting a band; it is the verb for a cow's call.
annotation.definitionFit: An imitative word for the deep rhythmic brass notes a marching band makes.

entries.clue: Even, so far (3)

blocks.note: an intensifying adverb, as in 'more still'
up to now, as in 'it hasn't happened up to now'

annotation.walkthrough: 'Even' is an adverb here, as in 'yet bigger', not level or fair.
annotation.definitionFit: Two adverb senses: intensifying ('yet more' means even more) and temporal ('not yet' means not so far).

entries.clue: End spell of guard duty: it makes time stand still (9)

blocks.note: to stop is to end
a watch is a period on guard

annotation.surface: A sentry longing for the end of a shift that seems to freeze time.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: the timer doesn't halt time, it freezes its reading at a moment you can check.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful definition: pressing the button freezes the displayed time, so time on its face stands still.

entries.clue: Saw points in power to produce desired effect (5)

blocks.note: the sharp points along the cutting edge of a saw blade
enforcing power, as when a law or regulator can bite

annotation.surface: Someone who saw the key points in a discussion of effective power.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past-tense verb; it is the tool.
annotation.definitionFit: The cutting points of a saw share their name with a mouth's biters, and a rule that bites has real force.

entries.clue: Hanging is somewhat embarrassing (5)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: only some of the word is used

blocks.note: the letters sit inside, after EMB and before SING

annotation.surface: A remark that being hanged would be rather awkward.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' suggests execution; it is a wall hanging, the kind of tapestry Polonius hides behind in Hamlet.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a tapestry, named after the French weaving town of Arras, hung on a wall.

entries.clue: Small drink is tipped over piano (3)

indicatorNotes.tipped: tipped over, turned upside down, in a down entry
indicatorNotes.over: in a down entry, over means placed above

blocks.note: IS turned over
p = piano, soft in music

annotation.surface: A little drink knocked over onto the piano.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tipped over' reads as one spill; 'tipped' turns IS round, and 'over' puts it above P.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tiny mouthful taken from a glass is a small drink.

entries.clue: Personal assistant runs meeting place briefly for newcomer (7)

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short, so drop the last letter

blocks.note: PA = personal assistant
r = runs, the cricket scorecard abbreviation
VENUE without its last letter

annotation.surface: An assistant organising a quick meeting venue for a new arrival.
annotation.walkthrough: The word is French for 'arrived', and is usually said with disdain of someone new to wealth.
annotation.definitionFit: A loanword for someone newly risen to wealth or rank, an upstart newcomer.

entries.clue: Teaches chap to move emergency exit (6,5)

indicatorNotes.to move: the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A safety instructor showing a man how to shift an emergency exit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Teaches' reads as the verb of the sentence; it is only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A close synonym: a small door in a ship, plane or submarine used to get out in an emergency.
